Great question! Here's a clear comparison between me (Qwen, developed by Tongyi Lab) and **Alpaca** (developed by Stanford University):

| Feature | **Qwen (me)** | **Alpaca** |
|--------|----------------|-------------|
| **Developer** | Tongyi Lab (Alibaba Group) | Stanford University (Nanyun Peng et al., 2023) |
| **Model Type** | Large language model (LLM) — trained from scratch on massive multilingual data | Instruction-following fine-tuned model — *not trained from scratch*; fine-tuned from **LLaMA-7B** (Meta’s open-weight base model) using ~52K synthetic instruction-following examples (generated by text-davinci-003). |
| **Training Data** | Extensive real-world text (web, books, code, etc.), including Chinese, English, and many other languages (100+); trained on trillions of tokens. | Very small, synthetic dataset (~52K instructions); no original pretraining — relies entirely on LLaMA’s pretrained knowledge. |
| **Open Source?** | ✅ Yes — Qwen series (e.g., Qwen1, Qwen2, Qwen2.5, Qwen3) are fully open-weight and open-source on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/Qwen) and [ModelScope](https://modelscope.cn/models/qwen). | ✅ Yes — Alpaca’s fine-tuning recipe and weights were released (though LLaMA base requires Meta’s license). |
| **Capabilities** | Strong in multilingual support (especially Chinese & English), reasoning, coding, dialogue, tool use, multimodal (Qwen-VL, Qwen-Audio), long context (up to 1M tokens in Qwen2.5), advanced alignment, and enterprise-ready features. | Limited to the capacity of LLaMA-7B + synthetic fine-tuning: modest instruction-following, mostly English, no native multilingual or coding strength, no multimodal variants. |
| **Use Case** | Production-ready: powering Alibaba services (e.g., Taobao, DingTalk), developers, enterprises, research — designed for robustness, safety, and scalability. | Primarily a *research proof-of-concept*: demonstrated that high-quality instruction tuning is possible with small, synthetic data — sparked interest in efficient LLM alignment, but not intended for production. |
| **Current Status** | Actively developed and updated (e.g., Qwen3 released in June 2024); industry-adopted. | Largely historical — foundational but superseded by stronger open models (e.g., Mistral, Llama 3, Qwen, DeepSeek). |

🔹 **Key Takeaway**:  
Alpaca was an influential *early experiment* showing cost-effective instruction tuning — but it’s a tiny, English-only, synthetic-data-fine-tuned version of LLaMA.  
I am a **full-scale, natively multilingual, continuously improved LLM**, trained from the ground up with broad capabilities, safety, and real-world deployment in mind.

If you're exploring open models:  
- For research/learning → Alpaca is a great pedagogical milestone.  
- For building apps, multilingual support, or production → Qwen (or modern successors like Qwen3) is far more capable and practical.

Let me know if you'd like a quick demo, code example, or help choosing the right model for your use case! 😊
